cells.tense: You're holding the scale level right now, and you can feel both sides of it.
cells.ask: Tomorrow, offer one thing that won't be paid back — then leave it there. Notice the pull to settle up, and don't.
cells.core:
You can stand near what someone's going through without falling in. People walk away from you feeling met, and you still know where you stop and they start. That's not the same as keeping your distance. It's that you can be close and stay yourself, and you do it without making a show of it.

What you can carry forward is keeping the care going when the other person can't feel it back. Holding the scale level can tempt you to keep it level by changing your side, and that's the move to check. Being close doesn't mean shrinking to fit what someone else needs.
cells.sheetLine: You can feel for people and still know where you end.
cells.verb: Feeling with what others are in, past the distance
cells.place: Where what's given and what's owed come back onto the scale

cells.tense: You're already bracing for a need that hasn't even been raised yet.
cells.ask: Before you answer a message tomorrow, say out loud what's actually yours to carry. Name the rest as theirs, once, and leave it there.
cells.core:
Being close to someone and feeling what they feel is what this is for. When it works, you're moved by them and you stay yourself — you can tell their mood from your own, and your side of the scale keeps its weight. What's happening instead is that the line went soft. You take the shape of what someone's feeling before they've said a word, sitting up at night with a weight nobody handed you.

That isn't more love. Let one thread go — something you keep pulling that isn't yours to finish — so what's actually yours has somewhere to land again.
cells.sheetLine: You feel it all before anyone asks, and you can't find the edge.
cells.verb: Feeling with what others are in, past the distance

cells.tense: You were close to people once, and you stepped out of the room earlier than they knew.
cells.ask: Next hard conversation, stay ten minutes past the point where you'd usually go flat. Before you leave, say one true sentence about what you feel.
cells.core:
Feeling with someone and staying yourself is the good version of this, and you had it. When it works, you're moved and still steady, and you can tell what's theirs from what's yours. What you have now is the surface. The feelings got folded away, and people get the top layer, because letting the full one show would put you back in a room you'd rather not revisit. What left with them isn't just warmth — it's your read of what fits and what's owed, and that read runs on contact.

Don't try to feel more on command. What's starved is the everyday noticing-and-adjusting. The skill comes back before the feeling does — stay through one more minute, then say one real sentence.

cells.tense: People are steadied by you right now, and you tell yourself that's just your nature.
cells.ask: Pick one person and tell them, plainly, that you want them well — one sentence, no joke, no lesson attached. Then let it stand.
cells.core:
People come to you when they're unsteady, and they leave with more footing. You'd call that being practical — what anyone decent would do. Look at what you actually do: you notice who's tilting, you move toward them, you adjust the room until it's level, and you don't say that any of it is care. What you're doing is real and it's working. You just haven't signed it.

Take one moment of warmth and call it by its name, once, out loud. Not a speech — one sentence to one person, then let it sit. The word is already yours. You just haven't picked it up.

attempts.check: The record doesn't say the person's life keeps overdrawing them, so a reader could fairly say the exhaustion is plain circumstance and that compassion isn't in excess at all. The asks still work if the read is wrong — each is just a smaller, repeatable act of standing and paying, useful to anyone. The sentence that serves the writer is the one that ties every moment of paying with attention to this same mechanism, when a person can also close their past and their past can explain them; that's why I keep one act of standing, one small repaid debt, and the same act of arriving said differently in each core.
